# Design assumptions

This simulation assumes:

- two independent, approximately equal-sized groups;
- a two-sided independent-samples $t$-test (Welch test) at $\alpha = .05$;
- normally distributed outcomes with equal population standard deviations;
- the specified effect size $d$ is the standardized mean difference, with a mean of $0$ in group 1 and $d$ in group 2.

Here, `N` is the **total** sample size. With unequal allocation after integer rounding, group sizes are set to `floor(N / 2)` and `ceiling(N / 2)`.

# Power simulation

```{r simulation}
set.seed(params$seed)

n_values <- seq(500, 1000, by = 100)
d_values <- seq(0.10, 0.50, by = 0.05)

simulate_power <- function(n_total, d, nsims = 10000) {
  n1 <- floor(n_total / 2)
  n2 <- ceiling(n_total / 2)

  rejected <- logical(nsims)

  for (i in seq_len(nsims)) {
    group1 <- rnorm(n1, mean = 0, sd = 1)
    group2 <- rnorm(n2, mean = d, sd = 1)

    test <- t.test(group2, group1, alternative = "two.sided", var.equal = FALSE)
    rejected[i] <- test$p.value < 0.05
  }

  mean(rejected)
}

power_grid <- expand.grid(N = n_values, d = d_values)
power_grid$power <- mapply(
  simulate_power,
  n_total = power_grid$N,
  d = power_grid$d,
  MoreArgs = list(nsims = params$nsims)
)

power_grid$N <- factor(power_grid$N)
power_grid$d_label <- sprintf("%.2f", power_grid$d)
power_grid <- power_grid[order(power_grid$d, power_grid$N), ]
```

# Results

```{r power-table}
display_table <- power_grid
levels(display_table$N) <- paste0("N = ", levels(display_table$N))

display_table <- reshape(
  display_table[, c("d", "N", "power")],
  idvar = "d",
  timevar = "N",
  direction = "wide"
)

names(display_table) <- sub("^power\\.", "N = ", names(display_table))
names(display_table)[1] <- "d"

display_table[-1] <- lapply(display_table[-1], function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x))

kable(display_table, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Simulated power by total sample size and Cohen's d")
```

## Power heatmap

```{r heatmap, fig.cap="Simulated statistical power across effect sizes and total sample sizes."}
ggplot(power_grid, aes(x = d, y = N, fill = power)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", power)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#FDE0DD", high = "#31A354", limits = c(0, 1),
                      labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                      name = "Power") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = d_values) +
  labs(x = "Cohen's d", y = "Total sample size (N)",
       title = "Simulated power for a two-sided Welch t-test") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

## Power curves

```{r power-curves, fig.cap="Power curves for selected total sample sizes."}
power_grid_continuous <- power_grid
power_grid_continuous$N_numeric <- as.numeric(as.character(power_grid_continuous$N))

ggplot(power_grid_continuous,
       aes(x = d, y = power, color = factor(N_numeric), group = N_numeric)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.80, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = d_values) +
  labs(x = "Cohen's d", y = "Statistical power",
       color = "Total N",
       title = "Power as a function of effect size and sample size") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

# Notes

- Power estimates are simulation-based and include Monte Carlo uncertainty.
- Increasing `params$nsims` reduces this uncertainty but increases runtime.
- At `r scales::comma(params$nsims)` simulations, the Monte Carlo standard error is at most approximately `r sprintf("%.3f", sqrt(0.25 / params$nsims))`.
